about: Orient Cables (India) Limited manufactures networking cables and passive networking products (LAN, optical fibre, specialty power cables, patch cords, keystone jacks) mainly for telecom, broadband, data centre and IT customers. It runs two plants at Bhiwadi, Rajasthan and a new Bengaluru plant (started May 2026), with installed capacity of 895,776 km of cables. It claims about 22.9% share of India's networking cable market in Fiscal 2026 and is a B2B supplier with exports to UAE, Qatar, USA, Australia and others.
sector: Wires & Cables (Networking, Optical Fibre and Specialty Cables)
headquarters: New Delhi (registered office); corporate office in Gurugram

other.name: Revenue from networking cables and solutions

objects.purpose: Capital expenditure for machinery, equipment and civil works at manufacturing facilities
Repayment or prepayment of certain outstanding borrowings
General corporate purposes (capped at 25% of fresh issue gross proceeds)

promoters.background: Vipul Nagpal, founder and Chairman and Managing Director, has over 20 years of experience in cable manufacturing. Garima Nagpal is Whole Time Director. The offer for sale of Rs 232 crore is by the two individual promoters and the two family trusts.

concentration.note: Fiscal 2026: largest customer 25.75%, top 5 customers 64.99%, top 10 customers 76.52% of revenue (84.00% in the June 2026 quarter). Networking cables were 78.23% of Fiscal 2026 revenue.

litigation_note: Against the company: 2 material civil proceedings totalling Rs 2.04 crore (Rs 20.40 million) and 1 statutory or regulatory proceeding. By the company: 1 criminal and 1 material civil proceeding of Rs 0.34 crore (Rs 3.38 million). A promoter group member (sister of promoter Vipul Nagpal) is listed as a wilful defaulter over Rs 5.03 crore (Rs 50.31 million) of loans of another entity, with the bank NOC awaited.
strengths: One of India's top four networking cable makers with about 22.9% market share in Fiscal 2026, in an industry with high entry barriers.
Revenue grew at about 33.5% a year over Fiscal 2024 to 2026, from Rs 658 crore to Rs 1,172 crore.
Diversified, customised product range across networking, optical fibre, specialty power cables and new EV and solar-related products.
Customers include two of the top three telecom companies by revenue; top ten customers have been served for over nine years on average.
Holds ETL, UL, CPR, TSEC, RDSO and BIS certifications, and exports to UAE, Qatar, USA, Australia and other countries.
Two plants at Bhiwadi near container depots plus a new Bengaluru plant; installed capacity of 895,776 km, with expansion planned.
High return ratios in recent years, with ROCE of 23.82% and RoNW of 25.84% in Fiscal 2026 (down from 41.13% and 37.26% in Fiscal 2024).
Experienced promoter-led management with over 20 years in cables.

risks.title: Heavy customer concentration
risks.detail: Top 10 customers gave 76.52% of Fiscal 2026 revenue (84.00% in the June 2026 quarter) and the largest customer alone gave 25.75%. Losing one could hurt sharply.

risks.title: Negative operating cash flow and rising debt
risks.detail: Operating cash flow was negative Rs 26.64 crore in Fiscal 2026 and Rs 9.79 crore in Fiscal 2025. Borrowings rose from Rs 36.73 crore to Rs 234.19 crore over Fiscal 2024 to 2026; net debt/EBITDA rose from 0.49 to 2.31 times.

risks.title: Falling returns and margins
risks.detail: RoNW fell from 37.26% to 25.84% and ROCE from 41.13% to 23.82% between Fiscal 2024 and 2026. EBITDA margin dropped to 8.23% in Fiscal 2026 from 10.17%.

risks.title: Working capital and receivables pressure
risks.detail: Net working capital days rose from 14 to 48 over Fiscal 2024 to 2026. Sales are largely on credit with terms up to 90 days.

risks.title: Promoter group member listed as wilful defaulter
risks.detail: Promoter's sister Radhika Julka is listed as a wilful defaulter on a Rs 50.31 million loan of Julka Sons; the company says it was repaid but the bank NOC is awaited.

risks.title: Raw material dependence
risks.detail: Top 10 suppliers provided 69.71% of primary raw materials in Fiscal 2026 and 74.91% in the June 2026 quarter, exposing costs and supply to price swings.

risks.title: Promoters keep control, past compliance lapses and weak credit history
risks.detail: Promoters hold 99.99% before the offer. Past CSR and Companies Act non-compliances, an environmental non-compliance at Unit II, and last CRISIL rating of B/Stable (issuer not cooperating) are disclosed.

risks.title: Capex orders not yet placed and new product risk
risks.detail: Rs 91.50 crore capex from proceeds has no orders placed yet. Expansion adds capacity for allied products despite underutilisation, and new lines (E-beam, EV charging, drones) are unproven.

notes: Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2025 are Standalone; Fiscal 2026 is Consolidated (subsidiary OCL Greentech formed May 2025).
